edges.description: Viremic systemic spread and infected-tissue innate immune activation drive the acute febrile illness.
Dissemination from the inoculation site produces the systemic rash-fever-arthralgia syndrome recorded in Yap and later outbreaks.
Bloodstream dissemination reaches joints and peripheral tissues, yielding the arthralgia component of acute ZIKV disease.
Systemic infection and innate immune activation explain myalgia during acute ZIKV illness.
Disseminated acute arboviral infection explains headache as a systemic symptom of the febrile illness.
Disseminated acute ZIKV infection explains non-purulent conjunctivitis as part of the classic rash-fever-arthralgia-conjunctivitis syndrome.
Outbreak and case-control data link ZIKV infection with later immune-mediated peripheral neuropathy, but the exact cross-reactive target has not been established.
Viremia in pregnancy precedes infection of decidual and chorionic cells that move virus into the fetal compartment.
